servicePage.box_title: The system shut down without closing
servicePage.box_in_job: The machine was working when it cut out: check the piece before going on.
servicePage.box_v_calm_t: Most likely: the power was cut at once
servicePage.box_v_calm_d: Up to the last reading everything was normal (CPU max {cpu} %, memory {ram} %, {temp} °C): no overload and no heat. So the most likely cause is that power stopped reaching the Pi (cable, plug, supply or meter) and not that the Pi failed. This is an estimate.
servicePage.box_v_stuck_t: Most likely: the service was already stuck before the cut
servicePage.box_v_stuck_d: The last reading showed something stuck: {thing}. A task that does not move for minutes leaves the Pi slow or unresponsive, and the cut came afterwards. It does not look like heat or memory (CPU max {cpu} %, memory {ram} %, {temp} °C).
servicePage.box_v_heat_d: It reached {temp} °C in the last {min} min. Check the ventilation and the heat sink of the Pi.
servicePage.box_v_load_t: The Pi was at its CPU limit
servicePage.box_v_load_d: The CPU was near {cpu} % in the last readings. A hang from load is possible; see which processes were heavy in the Processes section.
servicePage.box_v_memory_d: Memory reached {ram} %. A hang from lack of memory is possible.
servicePage.box_v_mixed_d: CPU up to {cpu} %, memory up to {ram} %, {temp} °C at most. Look at the charts and the lines below.
servicePage.box_v_without_data_d: The cut came very soon after power-on, or the black box did not manage to save readings.
servicePage.box_todo: So it does not happen again
servicePage.air_rule: Turns on with M3/M4 and turns off a few seconds after M5.
servicePage.mov_card_sub: Who may move the machine (jog, Workbench, Vision...) while a cut is running.
servicePage.mov_opt_nobody_d: During a live cut or while the bridge sends orders, the jog, the Workbench and Vision move nothing.
servicePage.mov_opt_me_d: Only a file job blocks, as in DWC. You can move by hand during a live cut. Machine settings stay protected.
servicePage.mov_release_d: without bridge orders: the jog, the Workbench and Vision can move again (if the live job is still open, they ask to confirm first). It is the first step; the second is "Finish after" in Live job, which closes the job. Less than 8 s is risky: a slow program can leave the machine still for a few seconds between passes.
servicePage.live_end_intro: When it counts as finished: at once when the program sends the end signal; if it does not, by idle time.
servicePage.live_end_note: of rest and no activity. It is the second step, after "Consider it free after" (Machine movement): it closes the live job record, counts hours and kWh up to the last activity and releases the block, without asking to confirm. It does not stop the machine. Keep it equal to or longer than the other time.
servicePage.box_charts_note: The last minutes before shutting down (saved data, not live). The live charts are in System health.
servicePage.box_now_d: This already happened. The Pi started again by itself, so you do not need to do anything to get back to normal. If the Duet board also lost power, home the machine before moving or cutting.
servicePage.box_now_hide: This notice stays until you press Hide. If it happens again, a new one appears.
servicePage.box_v_calm_s1: Check that the power cable of the Pi and the plug are firm and do not move when touched.
servicePage.box_v_calm_s2: Open Consumption and look at the chart for that hour: if the power drops to 0 at once, the power was cut; if it keeps reading, the Pi restarted by itself.
servicePage.box_v_calm_s3: Check in the meter app whether a schedule or timer turns that plug off.
servicePage.box_v_calm_s4: If it happens again, try another 5 V supply and cable, and do not share them with motors or the heated bed.
servicePage.box_v_stuck_s1: Look in Pi service for the process that was slow or not beating and restart it if it stays that way.
servicePage.box_v_stuck_s2: Check the bridge and the communication with the Duet: a long lock usually comes from an order that never finishes.
servicePage.box_v_stuck_s3: If it happens again, download this report and compare it with the service log at that hour.

It is marked with M118 P0 S"BRIDGE JOB START <name>" in its start G-code and M118 P0 S"BRIDGE JOB END" at the end (G-code bridge), or with the API operations job.start / job.end; it is kept in Activity and blocks the jog while it runs.

procDocs.ext_WorkshopRS485_what: The RS485 plugin process: it talks to servos and other Modbus devices over the serial ports of the Pi.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopRS485_how: It opens each configured bus, polls the devices in turns and publishes their state in the machine model; the RS485 page reads it from there. It keeps backups and a history of what it sees.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopRS485_depends: The RS485 plugin enabled in Settings > Plugins, free serial ports, and devices connected and powered.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopRS485_why: Because the RS485 plugin is enabled. If you stop it in Settings > Plugins this process stops with it.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopVision_what: The vision engine (OpenCV): it analyses camera images to measure parts, find marks and detect smoke.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopVision_how: It asks the camera relay for pictures only when someone needs them and drops the stream after 30 s without requests; it uses the saved calibration to turn pixels into millimetres.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopVision_depends: The Vision plugin enabled, the camera relay (Camera or Workbench plugin) and the camera calibration.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopVision_why: Because the Vision plugin is enabled; at rest it uses almost nothing (about 0.1 % CPU).
procDocs.ext_base_what: The SQLite database of the service: activity history, consumption, presets and received commands.
procDocs.ext_base_how: A single file on the Pi; the other processes write there and the pages query it through the API. It repairs itself if it finds badly saved dates.
procDocs.ext_base_depends: The disk of the Pi and the Workshop service; it needs no plugin.
procDocs.ext_base_why: Because the service always needs it to keep the history.
procDocs.ext_bridge_what: The program on the Pi that lets other programs (for example the laser software) send G-code to the Duet over the network, through the Telnet port.
procDocs.ext_bridge_how: It listens on the configured port, receives the G-code lines of each connected program and passes them to the Duet; it tells the page when a live job starts and ends.
procDocs.ext_bridge_depends: On the workshop-gcode-bridge service being installed and active on the Pi (installed with install.sh), on the network and on the port being free.
procDocs.ext_bridge_why: Because it is installed and enabled on the Pi. It is only needed to send live jobs from an outside program; if you do not use it, it can be stopped.
procDocs.interceptor_what: Watches the M3, M4 and M5 G-codes that go through the board as they happen.
procDocs.interceptor_why: Turns the air assist on only when the laser turns on and off a few seconds after M5, so nobody has to remember it.
procDocs.interceptor_fails: The air no longer turns on and off by itself; the laser keeps working the same. It restarts by itself.
procDocs.interceptor_uses: The DSF connection (code interception) and the air relay (output 7).
procDocs.interceptor_where: Automations > Automatic air with the laser.
procDocs.status_light_what: Paints the status zone of the LED strip and works out the indicator the screens show.
procDocs.status_light_why: Shows at a glance what the machine is doing (idle, job, pause, risk) with a colour and an effect, on the strip and in the bar.
procDocs.status_light_fails: The status LEDs keep the last colour or the board fallback takes over; the screens stop showing the indicator.
procDocs.status_light_uses: The board object model, the M150 commands and the rules of the Lights and status page.
procDocs.status_light_where: Lights and status page. It rests when that plugin is stopped.
procDocs.consumption_what: Reads the Tuya energy meter (W, V, A and accumulated kWh).
procDocs.consumption_why: Stores the consumption history so the cost per day, month or job can be worked out.
procDocs.consumption_fails: No new readings are saved; the chart shows a gap. What was already saved is kept.
procDocs.consumption_uses: The Tuya meter over the local network and the database.
procDocs.consumption_where: Power page (rate and meter). It rests when that plugin is stopped.
procDocs.jobs_what: Detects when a job starts and ends, the mode changes or the work zone changes.
procDocs.jobs_why: Feeds the Activity history, the phone alerts and the hours and energy per job.
procDocs.jobs_fails: Job starts and ends are not recorded; Activity and the alerts stop hearing about them.
procDocs.jobs_uses: The machine state (single subscription) and the database.
procDocs.motors_what: Works out the pulse frequency, RPM, speed and driver state of each motor.
procDocs.motors_why: Shows how close to its limit each motor works and whether a driver reports a problem.
procDocs.motors_fails: The Motors page stops updating. Movement is not affected.
procDocs.motors_uses: The object model, M122 and a read-only read of the GSTAT register.
procDocs.motors_where: Motors page. It rests when that plugin is stopped.
procDocs.jog_what: Moves the machine while a jog control is held.
procDocs.jog_why: Turns the knob, the arrows and the keyboard into short chained moves with the laser off.
procDocs.jog_fails: Jog stops moving; the rest of the machine is unaffected. If the screen heartbeat stops arriving, the movement cuts itself.
procDocs.jog_uses: Its own connection to the board and the motion owner.
procDocs.events_what: Watches the board messages: emergencies, pauses, errors and warnings.
procDocs.events_why: Stores them in Activity and sends them to the phone when needed.
procDocs.events_fails: Emergency, pause and error alerts are lost while it is stopped.
procDocs.events_uses: The object model messages (single subscription) and the notifier.
procDocs.trace_what: Records the path of the running job.
procDocs.trace_why: Lets Zones > Job draw the path. It only records while someone is watching; otherwise it sleeps.
procDocs.trace_fails: The job path is not drawn. The job itself is not affected.
procDocs.trace_uses: The object model (position) and files on the SD.
procDocs.health_what: Measures the Pi temperature, WiFi, services and power supply.
procDocs.health_why: Warns before something fails: high temperature, WiFi down, a stopped service or an unexpected reboot.
procDocs.health_fails: The Health page and its alerts stop updating.
procDocs.health_uses: System commands (vcgencmd, nmcli, systemctl) and the object model.
procDocs.camera_what: Shares the camera video with all screens and records the timelapses.
procDocs.camera_why: Prevents every screen from opening its own connection to the weak camera.
procDocs.camera_fails: The shared video and new timelapses are lost.
procDocs.camera_uses: The ESP32-CAM camera, ffmpeg and the SD.
procDocs.camera_where: Cameras tab of the Timelapses and captures page, in the Camera plugin.
procDocs.timer_what: Counts down the timed shutdown of the bar.
procDocs.timer_why: Turns everything off at the chosen time, without cutting a running job.
procDocs.timer_fails: The scheduled shutdown does not run.
procDocs.timer_uses: The system clock and the power cut.
procDocs.risk_what: Detects when something leaves the machine without a protection: calibrations and released motors.
procDocs.risk_why: Warns on screens and LEDs for as long as the risk lasts and clears itself when it ends.
procDocs.risk_fails: The risk is not announced. The board protections are unchanged.
procDocs.risk_uses: The object model and the flags set by the calibration macros.
procDocs.risk_where: No settings: it turns on when calibrating or releasing motors.
procDocs.config_guard_what: Watches the board start-up after a new configuration is saved.
procDocs.config_guard_why: Goes back to the previous configuration if the start-up fails or nobody confirms.
procDocs.config_guard_fails: A bad configuration would not be reverted by itself.
procDocs.config_guard_uses: The config.g backup and the board state.
procDocs.motion_what: Decides whether the machine may move or change its geometry, and why not.
procDocs.motion_why: Prevents two things from moving at once (jog, macros, job) and explains the block.
procDocs.motion_fails: The pages do not know whether a move is in progress and may allow too much or too little.
procDocs.motion_uses: The object model, the screen heartbeats and the bridge.
procDocs.motion_where: No settings: used by Jog, Zones and the macros.
procDocs.subscription_what: Keeps the single DSF subscription with the machine state.
procDocs.subscription_why: It is the source every other process reads from, so nobody asks the board for the state on its own.
procDocs.subscription_fails: The processes keep old data until it reconnects, which it does by itself.
procDocs.subscription_where: See patches/s and KB/s under 'Load this service puts on the Duet'.
procDocs.box_black_what: Writes a line every few seconds with load, CPU, RAM, temperature and state to the SD.
procDocs.box_black_why: If the Pi hangs or is switched off by force, there is a record of the last moments.
procDocs.box_black_fails: No trail is kept; after a hang the cause will not be known.
procDocs.box_black_uses: Files on the SD (two of 512 KB, rotating).
procDocs.ui_setting_moved: Each setting lives in the row of its process; only its state is shown here.
procDocs.ui_setting_no_row: The service does not publish that process yet
procDocs.set_air_what: A switch of the service: with it, the air assist turns on by itself when the laser turns on (M3/M4) and off a few seconds after M5.
procDocs.set_air_why: Nobody has to remember the air on every cut, and the delay avoids turning it off between two consecutive strokes.
procDocs.set_air_missing: Off, the air is only handled by hand or by the program that sends the job; the laser cuts the same.
procDocs.set_air_how: Turn the switch on and pick how many seconds the air stays on after M5. It needs a session with the operator role or higher.
procDocs.set_lights_what: The status zone of the LED strip: this process paints it by itself according to the mode and what the machine is doing.
procDocs.set_lights_why: Shows at a glance what the machine is doing (idle, job, pause, risk) with a colour and an effect, on the strip and in the bar.
procDocs.set_lights_missing: With the automatic off those LEDs are used by the work lighting and the screens stop showing the indicator.
procDocs.set_lights_how: It is turned on, off and configured in the Lights and status page (and in the quick buttons of the bar); here you only see the result.
procDocs.set_lights_no_plugin: The Lights plugin is not active: there is no page to open.
procDocs.set_zones_what: The main switch of the bed zones: with it, the service intercepts M140/M190 and shares the temperature out among the configured zones.
procDocs.set_zones_why: Lets you heat only the zones the part uses and apply the offset of each one, without changing the G-code.
procDocs.set_zones_missing: Off, M140 and M190 go through to the board as they are (one bed) and the zones stay unused; the configuration is kept.
procDocs.set_zones_how: Turn it on or off here; the zones, their offsets and the map are drawn in 3D printing > Bed zones. It needs a session with the technician role or higher.
procDocs.set_zones_unreadable: The configuration of the zones could not be read.
procDocs.set_zones_problems: The saved configuration has problems: the zones are not used until it is fixed in 3D printing.
procDocs.set_zones_conflict: Somebody changed the zones in the meantime: they were read again; try once more.
procDocs.auto_poweroff_what: When the job ends it turns everything off and cuts the machine power.
procDocs.auto_poweroff_when: When the running job ends, or the next one if there is none.
procDocs.auto_poweroff_note: It is only armed and disarmed here or in the side bar; it never cuts a running job. It cuts the power through the Tuya meter: make sure nothing must stay on.
procDocs.auto_poweroff_note_no_bar: It is only armed and disarmed here; it never cuts a running job. It cuts the power through the Tuya meter: make sure nothing must stay on.
procDocs.auto_job_what: Marks the live job sent by an external program through the G-code bridge.
procDocs.auto_job_when: It starts with the material macro (livemark.g) or the line M118 P0 S"BRIDGE JOB START name". It ends with M118 P0 S"BRIDGE JOB END", on stop or cancel, if the machine halts, or after the chosen rest time. Also with the job.start and job.end operations of the API.
procDocs.auto_job_note: The idle timeout closes a job that was left open and adds its hours and kWh. While there is one, jog and zones are locked so nothing moves the machine in the middle of the cut.
procDocs.ui_cadence_help: Average time between heartbeats compared with what is expected. Up to 100 % is normal; above it the process is falling behind.
procDocs.ui_summary_unavailable: Not available: the service is not connected
procDocs.guard_what: Checks that the safety processes keep beating: status lights, camera relay, board events, motion, risk, health, Vision and RS485.
procDocs.guard_why: If one dies the protection disappears unnoticed and the light strip could stay green with the machine in fault.
procDocs.guard_fails: Nobody watches the watchers: the status lights show the warning if this process stops.
procDocs.guard_uses: This service's heartbeats, the answer of Vision and the RS485 data.
procDocs.guard_where: API operations guard.status and guard.set (the safe action is to warn or to pause the job).
procDocs.ui_group_safety_desc: They protect the machine. They are shown and watched; they cannot be switched off from here.
procDocs.ui_group_machine_desc: They move or switch on something on the machine.
procDocs.ui_group_data_desc: They read, measure and save. If they fail you lose data or screens, not safety.
procDocs.ui_group_support_desc: They make the rest work: shared state, publishing, communication.
procDocs.ui_group_ext_desc: System processes the service does not control, it only checks them.
procDocs.ui_locked_note: Protected: it is shown and watched, but it has no switch.
procDocs.ui_mode_pending: Pending restart: you chose "{mode}" and it keeps running until the service restarts.
procDocs.ui_mode_audit: Changes made here are recorded in the audit log (Audit, read by administrators).
procDocs.ui_pending_text: These changes apply when the service restarts. If nobody can restart it from here yet, restart it from DWC (Settings > Plugins) or wait for the next update.
procDocs.ui_ctl_limits: The pause lasts until you resume it or the service restarts (it is not saved). The restart is requested and the loop starts again on its next pass.
procDocs.ui_paused_detail: Paused by a person: it collects no data until you resume it or the service restarts. It does not count as late.
procDocs.ui_done_pause: Paused. The process notices it on its next pass: it may take up to {n} to stop collecting data.
procDocs.ui_done_resume: Resumed. It collects data again on its next pass (up to {n}).
procDocs.ui_done_restart: Restart requested. The process relaunches on its next pass (up to {n}).
procDocs.ui_paused_banner_text: They collect no data until you resume them or the service restarts. Open the row and press Resume.
procDocs.ui_restart_stuck: It did not respond: if it stays like this, restart the service.
procDocs.ui_proc_failed: The action could not be completed: {msg}
procDocs.ui_svc_restart_hint: Restarts the whole service with the machine at rest; the protections are off for a few seconds.
procDocs.ui_svc_slow: Taking longer than usual: check Settings > Plugins.
procDocs.ui_svc_failed: The service could not be restarted: {msg}
procDocs.ui_pending_text_can: These changes apply when the service restarts. You can restart it from here when the machine is at rest.
procDocs.guardian_laser_what: If laser power is left set with no job running, it sends M5 to turn it off.
procDocs.guardian_laser_why: A laser left on by a cut-off program or a failed command can mark the part when the machine moves; this guardian turns it off by itself.
procDocs.guardian_laser_fails: The laser may stay on if something fails.
procDocs.guardian_laser_uses: The Laser mode of the machine and the connection with the board (the shared state and sending M5).
procDocs.guardian_laser_where: Nobody reads it: it acts by itself. It is a protection and has no switch.
procDocs.intercept_watchdog_what: If an intercepted G-code takes longer than 20 s to resolve, it releases the channel and restarts the service.
procDocs.intercept_watchdog_why: A stuck code holds back every other one on the channel and the DWC buttons stay on "sending" until DSF is restarted.
procDocs.intercept_watchdog_fails: A stuck G-code can leave the machine not answering.
procDocs.intercept_watchdog_where: DSF: when the service restarts, DSF starts it again.
procDocs.watchdog_lock_what: If the lock of the bridge with the board is held for more than 20 s, it dumps the stacks of all threads to the log.
procDocs.watchdog_lock_why: A lock that is never released freezes the service without a trace; the stacks of the threads show who holds it.
procDocs.watchdog_lock_fails: A bridge lock is not recorded and it is hard to tell what caused it.
procDocs.watchdog_lock_uses: The lock of the bridge with the board.
procDocs.publisher_what: It is the only thread that writes the data the pages show.
procDocs.publisher_why: Writing from a single thread keeps several processes from stepping on the same data and keeps the pages consistent.
procDocs.publisher_fails: The pages stop updating and show the last data published.
procDocs.publisher_uses: What the other processes leave to be published.
procDocs.communication_what: It emits the state of the communication with the board every 10 s.
procDocs.communication_why: The pages and the notices need to know which channel is used to talk to the board and whether it is free.
procDocs.communication_fails: The communication signal is lost: the pages do not know which channel is in use.
procDocs.communication_uses: The configured G-code channels and their state.
procDocs.communication_where: Communication with the board on this page and the notices of the other pages.
procDocs.subscription-demand_what: It waits until some process needs the machine state, then opens the single subscription to DSF.
procDocs.subscription_demand_what: It waits until some process needs the machine state, then opens the single subscription to DSF.
procDocs.subscription-demand_why: This way no subscription is kept open when nobody uses it.
procDocs.subscription_demand_why: This way no subscription is kept open when nobody uses it.
procDocs.subscription-demand_fails: If it does not open the subscription, the processes that read the machine state get no data.
procDocs.subscription_demand_fails: If it does not open the subscription, the processes that read the machine state get no data.
procDocs.subscription-demand_uses: Some process asking for the machine state; the connection with DSF.
procDocs.subscription_demand_uses: Some process asking for the machine state; the connection with DSF.
procDocs.subscription-demand_where: The Machine state (subscription) process and everything that reads it.
procDocs.subscription_demand_where: The Machine state (subscription) process and everything that reads it.
procDocs.commands_extra_what: It moves the commands that other plugins write to a file into the Received commands history.
procDocs.commands_extra_why: The commands of other plugins (for example RS485) also appear in the history.
procDocs.commands_extra_fails: The commands of other plugins stop appearing in Received commands.
procDocs.commands_extra_uses: The file each plugin writes and the database.
procDocs.base_backup_what: It makes the daily backup of the database.
procDocs.base_backup_why: If the database is damaged or erased, the last copy can be restored.
procDocs.base_backup_fails: There is no daily backup: whatever is saved after the last copy has no backup.
procDocs.base_backup_uses: The database and the free space on the disk or the chosen USB stick.
procDocs.api_what: It serves the HTTP API of the service.
procDocs.api_why: It is the door the pages, the API keys and other applications talk through.
procDocs.api_fails: The pages and applications that use the API can no longer talk to the service.
procDocs.api_uses: The HTTP port of the service and the permissions of each role.
procDocs.api-macros_what: It serves the macro mailbox: the orders the machine macros leave for the service.
procDocs.api_macros_what: It serves the macro mailbox: the orders the machine macros leave for the service.
procDocs.api-macros_why: It lets a macro of the board ask the service for something without going through HTTP.
procDocs.api_macros_why: It lets a macro of the board ask the service for something without going through HTTP.
procDocs.api-macros_fails: The macros that depend on the service get no answer.
procDocs.api_macros_fails: The macros that depend on the service get no answer.
procDocs.api-macros_uses: The macro mailbox and the API of the service.
procDocs.api_macros_uses: The macro mailbox and the API of the service.

roles.title: Roles and permissions
roles.lead: Who can do what. The four base roles are fixed; here you create own roles with more or fewer permissions.
roles.guide_what: The table shows each capability (a group of service operations) and what every role allows. An own role starts from a base role and adds or removes capabilities.
roles.guide_why: To give a person only what they need: for example an operator who can also power off, or a technician who cannot calibrate the height.
roles.guide_missing: Without own roles there are only four levels and each one inherits everything of the one below.
roles.guide_how: Press New role or the pencil of an own role, tap a cell of its column to grant it, deny it or inherit again, check the difference and apply. Then assign the role in the people table.
roles.users_off: Today everybody is an administrator: users are switched off or there are none yet, so roles do not apply. Switch them on in the people card.
roles.damaged: The file of own roles is damaged: no own role is known and whoever has one can only stop. An administrator must repair or delete it by hand on the server.
roles.matrix_help: In an own role, tap a cell to switch it: inherit from the base role, grant or deny. The other cells cannot be changed.
roles.saved: Role saved. It applies from the next action of whoever has it.
roles.switch_block: Apply or discard the changes of the role you are editing before moving to another.
roles.cell_allowed_why: The base role allows every operation of this capability.
roles.cell_partial_why: The base role allows only some operations of this capability.
roles.cell_blocked_why: The base role does not allow this capability. An own role can grant it.
roles.cell_limited_why: Allowed only in the modes of the operator, or with the camera switched on for the visitor.
roles.cell_granted_why: The own role adds this capability to those of its base role.
roles.cell_denied_why: The own role removes it even if its base role allows it. A denial always wins.
roles.cell_locked_why: Only the administrator has it: users, roles, keys, passwords and critical changes cannot be delegated.
roles.cell_stop_why: It includes stopping, and stopping is never blocked: it cannot be denied.
roles.foreign_kept: This role also has {n} entries by operation name that the table does not show; they are kept as they are.
roles.diff_new_plain: No changes over the base role {base}. Tap cells of the new column to grant or deny.
roles.risky_warning: You are granting high-risk capabilities: {list}. They can damage the hardware or lock the workshop out.
roles.block_name: Write a name of 1 to 32 letters, digits, spaces, dots or hyphens.
roles.eff_help: Choose a person or a role and see, operation by operation, what they can do and the reason of every block.
roles.eff_choose: Choose a person or a role
roles.src_grant: By a grant of the own role
roles.help_custom_what: A role created by the administrator: it starts from a base role and adds or removes capabilities.
roles.help_custom_why: To give each person just what they need, without handing over the whole next level.
roles.help_custom_how: New role, choose the base role, tap cells of its column and apply. Then assign it to a person.
roles.help_base_what: Visitor, operator, technician or administrator: the four fixed levels of the workshop. Each includes the one below.
roles.help_base_why: An own role inherits everything from its base; only what you grant or deny changes. The administrator cannot be a base.
roles.help_base_how: Choose the base closest to what the person needs and adjust from there.
roles.help_granted_what: A capability the own role adds even though its base role does not have it.
roles.help_granted_why: To give a single permission, such as powering off the workshop, without moving the person up a level.
roles.help_granted_how: Tap a not-allowed cell of an own role. High-risk ones call for care.
roles.help_denied_what: A capability the own role removes even though its base role has it. A denial beats everything else.
roles.help_denied_why: So a person cannot do one specific thing, such as calibrating the height, without losing the rest.
roles.help_denied_how: Tap an allowed cell of an own role. Stopping can never be denied.
roles.help_locked_what: Capabilities only the administrator has: people, roles, keys, passwords and critical changes.
roles.help_locked_why: Delegating them would let anyone change who gets in or delete the workshop data.
roles.help_locked_how: They cannot be touched. For these you need to be an administrator.

shared.service_notice_show: How the system talks to the Duet
shared.service_notice_explain_1: The system sends its G-code to the Duet through DSF: the board in SBC mode, joined to the system by the flat cable. The system service (the WorkshopService plugin) serves the workshop pages: it reads the data, paints the lights and moves the jog.
shared.service_notice_explain_2: Without SBC mode (the Duet alone, with a PanelDue or its own WiFi) there is no DSF and the service cannot run. With SBC mode, the service is installed and started in Settings > Plugins.
shared.service_notice_explain_3: Inside the Duet every G-code origin has its own channel (its own queue). Which channel each workshop feature uses is chosen in System service, in the Communication with the Duet card.
shared.service_notice_no_sbc_text: This page needs the Duet in SBC mode with the system service (WorkshopService). Without that it cannot work.
shared.service_notice_missing_text: The WorkshopService plugin is missing. Install it so this page can work.

shared.startup_row_mode_laser_what: A macro that prepares the machine for laser mode: tool, heaters and settings of that mode.
shared.startup_row_mode_laser_for: The Tool change tab runs it when you switch the machine to this mode.

shared.startup_row_mode_cnc_what: A macro that prepares the machine for CNC mode: tool, heaters and settings of that mode.
shared.startup_row_mode_cnc_for: The Tool change tab runs it when you switch the machine to this mode.

shared.startup_q_method: How does your machine enter this mode?
shared.startup_q_method_tip: Pick the closest one. If you are not sure, pick "A macro of mine" and write the path of one you already have.
shared.startup_opt_tool: By selecting a tool (the one of your config.g)
shared.startup_q_tool_tip: The T number you declared with M563 in your config.g. Do not guess: check your config.g.
shared.startup_q_macro_tip: It starts with 0:/ and ends in .g, for example 0:/macros/mode/my-mode.g. The assistant only calls it, it does not create it.
shared.startup_row_modefile_tip: Each mode keeps its speeds, limits and the command that turns it on in its own file. It is already created and fully commented, with explanations: edit it or use "Create with help". If your machine has no such head, tap "Do not use this".
shared.startup_row_modefile_what: The file with the settings of this mode: how fast the machine may move, how far the work area reaches and the command that puts the machine in that mode.
shared.startup_row_modefile_for: Every time the machine enters this mode this file runs. Without it the machine uses generic values and may try to move faster or farther than yours can.
shared.startup_row_modefile_missing: It is all commented, so the machine applies no setting in this mode. Open it and uncomment what applies, or use "Create with help". If you do not have this head, tap "Do not use this".
shared.startup_q_speed: How fast do you want it to move?
shared.startup_q_speed_tip: Start with "gentle": it is slow and safe. Raise it by hand in the file later, once you know what your machine can take.
shared.startup_q_limit_tip: How far the work area reaches from zero, in millimetres. Measure it on your machine: a number that is too big makes it try to go where there is nothing.
shared.startup_q_pin: Which output is the laser power signal connected to?
shared.startup_q_pin_tip: The name of the board output where you connected the laser power wire, for example out9. Look at your wiring or your config.g.
shared.startup_row_boot_tip: For the machine to enter its mode by itself when it turns on, the last line of sys/config.g has to call automodeselect.g. This row only checks it; it does not edit config.g.
shared.startup_row_boot_what: A line at the end of sys/config.g that tells the machine to apply the saved mode when it turns on.
shared.startup_row_boot_for: Without it the machine starts in no mode and the settings of each mode are not applied until somebody taps a mode button.
shared.startup_row_boot_missing: Open sys/config.g with DWC's editor and add this line at the end: M98 P"0:/sys/workshop/modes/automodeselect.g" . Save and restart the board.
shared.startup_boot_missing: the line is missing in config.g
shared.startup_row_unmigrated: Mode files moved to the new place
shared.startup_row_unmigrated_tip: The mode files (modefff.g, modelaser.g, modecnc.g, automodeselect.g, modestate.g) must be in sys/workshop/modes and sys/workshop/data. The pages read only the new place. Apply the group of mode files in the start-up wizard (Puesta en marcha).
shared.startup_row_unmigrated_what: The mode files of this machine are still in sys/ (old place). The start-up wizard moves them and fixes the lines that call them.
shared.startup_row_unmigrated_for: Until they are moved, this page sees no modes and cannot check or edit their settings.
shared.startup_row_unmigrated_missing: Modes not migrated: open the start-up wizard of the service (Puesta en marcha), tick the group of mode files, read the diffs and apply it with the machine off.
shared.startup_unmigrated_ok: the mode files are in the new place
shared.startup_miss_unmigrated: The mode files are still in the old place (sys/): apply the start-up wizard to move them.

shared.startup_row_modes_for: A machine that only prints does not need mode macros. If you also use a laser or a spindle, each mode needs its macro and its settings file so the machine can switch between them.
